text:
olivia: ACME POC stuck, getting 403 with \"invalid_project\" when calling /v1/chat. They pasted the request below.

ryan: paste the curl so we can inspect headers.

olivia: here it is:

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: org-acme' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: proj-demo' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-chat-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}] }'

mia: two quick things — 1) if the key is project-scoped, X-Redwood-Project takes precedence; if the key is org-scoped, send X-Redwood-Org. Mixing both can trigger validation errors. 2) shadow/trial keys sometimes are bound to a different org.

ops-bot: NOTE: audit id 2026-07-11-ACME-POC created for this thread. Avoid posting full keys/screenshots. Redact tokens.

ryan: check the key metadata: you can call the console read-only endpoint to see owner org without exposing the secret:

curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_lookup_...REDACTED' https://console.redwood.ai/v1/keys/lookup?token=sk_live_XXXX

mia: if lookup shows the key is project-scoped under proj-other, that explains invalid_project. Also validate scopes: missing generate/chat scope will surface as authz.scope_missing:chat in logs.

olivia: they said the key came from an email and they're not sure which workspace. their SDK auto-populates both headers which probably caused conflict.

ryan: tell them to try two quick repros: 1) Remove X-Redwood-Org header, keep X-Redwood-Project -> expect 200 if key maps to that project. 2) Remove X-Redwood-Project, keep X-Redwood-Org -> expect 200 if key is org-scoped. Post results.

sec-bot: SECURITY REMINDER: when sharing console screenshots, blur any key and session ids. Use role-limited support tokens for lookups.

olivia: customer tried option 1 (removed org header) and still got 403 but log shows authz.scope_missing:chat. they had a read-only trial key.

mia: that matches — trial keys often lack chat/generate scopes. Ask them to create a new service key in the project with the chat scope from Console -> Project -> API keys.

olivia: they created a project service key with chat scope and now calls succeed. :white_check_mark:

ryan: good. follow-up: we'll add a tiny troubleshooting blurb to the POC playbook: - header precedence (project vs org) - how to lookup key binding - common error strings (invalid_project, invalid_key, authz.scope_missing) - don't post secrets.

mia: i'll draft the blurb and share a short checklist for presales demos (include exact curl examples and what to check when customers see 403). closing POC once doc is sent.

ops-bot: POC ticket updated: status -> resolved.

olivia: thanks all!
